# @pogrobert/surfaces

> Art drawn by code, not by an image model, for every picture a site repeats: post covers, link previews, docs and changelog headers, empty states, episode art, slides and profile headers. Make a brand once, from a colour or from the site's own HTML and CSS; every cover then follows from its title, the same bytes forever. It is for pictures a site repeats; a picture of one particular thing is a photo's job. A wrong input throws an error that names the fix.

Rules for writing code with it are in AGENTS.md. In short: `const brand = createBrand({ name: "acme.dev", ...readPage(html, css) })`, then `brand.cover({ title })`, `brand.og({ title })`, `brand.hero`, `brand.card`, `brand.banner({ for: "x" })`, drawn by `toHtml`, `toSvg`, or `toJpeg`/`toPng` (from `/png`). The images are art and carry no words: the site sets its titles in its own font over `scene.areas[0]`, as `<Cover brand={brand} title={title} />` (from `/react`) does by itself, and `drawTitle: true` draws one into an image file that has to carry it. `generate(input)` is the lower level, for one exact cover.

## Where things come from

- `@pogrobert/surfaces`: `createBrand`, `readPage`, `directions`, `generate`, `validate`, `catalog`, `describe`, `toSvg`, `toHtml`, `loadFont`, `formats`, `inputSchema`
- `@pogrobert/surfaces/png`: `toJpeg`, `toPng` (install `@resvg/resvg-js`, or `@resvg/resvg-wasm` on an edge runtime), `toPngInBrowser`. Their bytes go straight into `new Response(bytes)`
- `@pogrobert/surfaces/react`: `<Cover>`, `<Surface>`
- `@pogrobert/surfaces/dom`: `mount`, `watch`
- `@pogrobert/surfaces/http`: `createHandler`, `signUrl`

## What trips agents up

- `<Cover brand title />` shows the title on the art itself, at a title's size, in the page's font. Don't add the same title beside it. To make it the page's heading, pass `<h1>{title}</h1>` as children. For art alone, `text="none"`; in a list, `use="card"`.
- `brand.cover` is the use `"post"`: `brand.input("post", { title })` is its input. To change one cover's size, shape or motion, spread it: `generate({ ...brand.input("post", { title }), width: 800, height: 800 })`. A cover's own options are only `title`, `id`, `tag`, `text` and `drawTitle`; anything else throws and says where it belongs.
- One `color`, as hex. The second colour on a cover is chosen from it; there is no second colour, no background and no transparent ground to give.
- `scene.areas[0]` is in pixels of the output, with the `ink` that reads there. `ink` is CSS: under `theme: "auto"` it is a `var(…)`, so an image renderer such as Satori takes `scene.ink`, always hex.
- An image file has one theme. A brand's link preview and headers are light even when the brand follows the reader (`theme: "auto"`); any other cover in both themes can't be a PNG or JPEG until it is drawn in one.
- Only `toHtml` moves, and only styles with `moves: true` in `catalog`; `brand.hero` loops by itself where its style does. A loop needs a pause control: `data-paused` on the cover, `paused` on `<Surface>`, or `pause()` from `mount`.
- `mood` is `"calm"` or `"bold"`, the quiet or loud end of a style; left out, the seed ranges over both. `grain: "smooth"` is a little grain, never none.
- A title drawn into an image is read out to screen readers; art alone is hidden. `describe(scene, { title })` writes `og:image:alt`.

## Docs

- [AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md): the rules, under 1 KB
- [README.md](README.md): examples for React, OG images, DOM, SVG and HTTP
- [docs/api.md](docs/api.md): the whole API and why each part is there

## Reference

- [dist/schema.json](dist/schema.json): the input as JSON Schema (also `inputSchema`)
- `catalog`: every style with what it looks like, what it suits, its shapes, and whether it moves
- `directions(choices)`: several varied, checked brands to show a person; keep the chosen one's `look`
- `npx @pogrobert/surfaces init`: reads the site, writes its brand, an AGENTS.md block and the link preview; `kit` writes the link preview and social headers (never icons); `preview` and `check` to look and verify
- `readPage(html, css, design?)`: the facts a brand chooses its look from: colours, background, dark mode, fonts, words; a DESIGN.md given third comes first
- `logo` on a brand: its own logo, set as it is on link previews and headers
- `validate(input)`: every problem with a `generate` input, each with its fix, without drawing
